It retains the complete before tuple, performs the existing bounded filesystem copy, samples the complete after tuple, writes both compared tuples0400 before any equality refusal, and requires exact equality. After success it immediately writes `raw/snapshot-handoff.json`0400 containing both live tuples, the copied main/WAL/SHM SHA256+length identities and UTC window/handoff times. A changed input DURING copying still STOPs with no retry. Existing full-copy checks, byte/size caps, aliases, and all raw copies remain. The handoff records the consistency boundary; it claims no DB/assets cross-file atomicity.

The production seal's reader copy, normal WAL-aware read-only scan and backup work only on detached OWNED files. Its later guard compares raw main/WAL/SHM byte identities against the handoff, plus unchanged reader/backup logical equivalence. It no longer re-hashes or requires a later live source to equal that historical snapshot. This exception is only for the explicitly selected production seal. Every OWNED-source seal still requires its source's full original tuple to remain equal through its scan, and all raw-master preservation predicates remain.

The asset copy has its own before/copy/after-equal window and copied byte-identity check. It writes its separate0400 `assets-snapshot-handoff.json` OUTSIDE the asset tree, so metadata is not injected into runtime asset inputs. The DB and asset handoff UTCs are recorded separately in the baseline and final receipt, explicitly without cross-file atomicity. Assets remain runtime inputs for the two stopped startups, not scientific evidence. Terminal owned asset preservation compares the retained asset master to that asset handoff, not an earlier unrelated live inventory.

After the fresh DB seal and asset copy, and again after terminal physical accounting or on refusal, the controller records bounded `lstat`-only live DB/WAL/SHM and asset-root/file/directory metadata. These records are explicitly observational, contain no content hashes or SQL, and never serve as snapshot authority or equality STOP conditions. Missing later files/roots are recorded as unavailable; bounded incomplete observations are labelled incomplete. Later legitimate producer evolution therefore does not invalidate the already established handoff. The predecessor's healthy identity/mount/flags/starttime checks remain unchanged.

Live equality failures now retain the exact compared states before raising: file opened identity, file before/after hashing metadata, source growth during copying, expected versus copied SHA/length, full DB-triple window, full asset-tree window and asset-copy identities. All evidence is0400, exclusive-create and retained. Availability/alias/type guards still refuse unsafe input. No later diagnostic is relabelled as an original after-sample.

At EVERY `Disk.check` budget checkpoint, before the reserve predicate, the controller records its actual cgroup-v2 `memory.stat` anonymous and file counters, all returned counters, the cgroup path, required reserve, active stage and monotonic time in an immutable owned JSON file. Counter parsing requires bounded ASCII/unique keys/nonnegative integers/anon+file fields. The source reads counters only and changes no limit, swap, heap or kernel setting. The earlier page-cache explanation is Claudio's inference, not a measurement of the failed unit. New actual-host guard verification demonstrates this interface from its own verification-session cgroup; it is not a060000 or070000 controller memory sample.
